policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the qere, which is what MACULA Hebrew projects; the alternative is the ketiv written in the Leningrad Codex.

decisions.evidence: ASV 16:13 'thy raiment was of fine linen' renders the word for fine linen with no feature that separates qere שֵׁשׁ from ketiv ששי; both are the same noun and the English cannot distinguish the spellings. No mapped textual note.

ASV 16:13 'thou didst eat' is second feminine singular, which both readings supply: qere אָכָלְתְּ is the normalized 2fs and ketiv אכלתי the archaic 2fs written with yod, common in Ezekiel. The English fixes person and gender, not the spelling.

ASV 16:18 'didst set' continues the 2fs address ('thou tookest', 'coveredst'); qere נָתַתְּ and ketiv נתתי are both 2fs, the ketiv being the archaic -תי spelling. The English does not distinguish them.
ASV 16:20 'Were thy whoredoms a small matter' is plural, matching qere מִתַּזְנוּתָיִךְ (plural with 2fs suffix) against the singular ketiv מתזנתך.
ASV 16:22 'thou hast not remembered' is 2fs; qere זָכַרְתְּ and ketiv זכרתי are both 2fs forms of the same verb, the ketiv the archaic -תי spelling. Nothing in the English selects a spelling.
ASV 16:25 'and multiplied thy whoredom' is singular, matching ketiv תזנתך (singular with 2fs suffix) rather than the plural qere תַּזְנוּתָיִךְ.

ASV 16:31 'makest thy lofty place' is 2fs; qere עָשִׂית and ketiv עשיתי are both 2fs, the ketiv the archaic -תי spelling. The only note here is classed alternative_rendering ('Or, that scoffeth at her hire') and concerns English wording, not the reading.
ASV 16:31 'hast not been' is 2fs; qere הָיִית and ketiv הייתי are both 2fs of היה, the ketiv archaically spelled. The verse's note is alternative_rendering and does not bear on the reading.
ASV 16:43 'thou hast not remembered' is 2fs; qere זָכַרְתְּ and ketiv זכרתי are both 2fs, differing only in the archaic yod spelling. The note is alternative_rendering and settles nothing textual.

ASV 16:43 'thou shalt not commit this lewdness' keeps the 2fs address; qere עָשִׂית and ketiv עשיתי are both 2fs. The alternative_rendering note ('Or, hast thou not committed etc.?') is about English phrasing.
ASV 16:47 'nor done after their abominations' addresses 'thou'; qere עָשִׂית and ketiv עשיתי are both 2fs forms, the ketiv archaically written. No note is mapped here.
ASV 16:51 'hast justified thy sisters' is plural, matching qere אֲחוֹתַיִךְ (plural with 2fs suffix) against the singular ketiv אחותך.
ASV 16:51 'which thou hast done' is 2fs; qere עָשִׂית and ketiv עשיתי are both 2fs, differing only in the archaic spelling. Nothing in the English chooses.

ASV 16:53 'their captivity' renders the noun alike under either spelling: שְׁבוּת (qere) and שבית (ketiv) are the same word for captivity. The verse note is alternative_rendering ('Or, return to') and bears on the verb, not this reading.
ASV 16:53 'the captivity of Samaria and her daughters' does not distinguish שְׁבוּת from שבית; the two spellings render identically in English. The mapped note is alternative_rendering.
ASV 16:53 'and the captivity of thy captives' shows the conjunction but nothing separating וּשְׁבוּת from ושבית, which are the same noun spelled two ways. The note is alternative_rendering.
ASV 16:59 'I will also deal with thee' is first person singular, matching qere וְעָשִׂיתִי; the ketiv ועשית would be second feminine singular ('and thou shalt deal'), which the ASV does not render.
